title: Long-lived GCP service-account JSON key used by CI to publish container images
severity_rationale: A static, non-expiring cloud credential stored as a GitHub repo secret in a public repository's workflow; its blast radius (which SA, which roles) is explicitly unverified by the repo's own credential manifest. Exposure requires a workflow or runner compromise, so not High; the deploy job already uses keyless WIF, so this is a residual legacy path.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:364-368 — uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2 / with: credentials_json: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:310 — PUBLISH_IMAGES: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) }}
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:43 — GCP_PROJECT_ID: lux-realestate-app
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:461-466 — Authenticate to Google Cloud (Workload Identity Federation, no key) ... workload_identity_provider: ${{ vars.BM_GCP_WIF_PROVIDER }}

docs/build/security/credential-manifest.yaml:~241 — kind: gcp-service-account-json-key ... rotation_class: gcp-sa-key-legacy ... 'Retire, do not rotate' ... 'Which service account backs it is unverified.'
preconditions: Push to main or a v* tag triggers build-images with PUBLISH_IMAGES=true; the secret GCP_SA_KEY exists in the repo settings.
expected: Image publishing authenticates with short-lived WIF tokens from a least-privilege pusher identity, like the deploy job.
observed: build-images authenticates with a static JSON key; the deploy job uses WIF. The manifest records that the key's backing SA and roles are unverified and that the project id (lux-realestate-app) is shared with another application name.
impact: Compromise of the Actions environment (malicious dependency in pnpm install during a main push, runner compromise, or a maintainer-approved malicious PR merged to main) exfiltrates a non-expiring credential able to push images to the registry that sandbox deploys pull from; roles beyond registry push cannot be excluded from code.
recommended_fix: Switch build-images to google-github-actions/auth with workload_identity_provider + a dedicated pusher service account (the manifest names bm-sbx-fnd-pusher), delete GCP_SA_KEY from GitHub and the key from IAM, and verify with one green main push.
acceptance_test: grep -n credentials_json .github/workflows/*.yml returns nothing; a main push publishes images with the WIF step and the GCP IAM console shows zero user-managed keys on the pusher SA.

title: Governance decision endpoint records a caller-supplied reviewer_user_id with no authentication (mode-gated to demo/development)
severity_rationale: Unauthenticated human-approval write would be High if reachable in sandbox/production; the in-process boot guard refuses those modes for this service, and compose only starts governance under the 'legacy' profile, so exploitability is confined to development stacks. Kept at Medium because the guard is a configuration-time inventory, not a code fix, and the endpoint resolves escalations that gate private-data disclosure.
evidence: brandme-governance/governance_console/main.py:40-43 — class GovernanceDecisionRequest(BaseModel): approved: bool / reviewer_user_id: str / note: str

brandme-governance/governance_console/main.py:119-120 — @app.post("/governance/escalations/{scan_id}/decision") async def resolve_escalation(scan_id: str, payload: GovernanceDecisionRequest, request: Request):

brandme-governance/governance_console/main.py:147-151 — transaction.update(table="AuditLog", columns=["audit_id", "human_approver_id", "escalated_to_human", "decision_summary"], values=[(audit_id, payload.reviewer_user_id, False, new_summary)])
brandme-governance/governance_console/main.py:71-72 — @app.get("/governance/escalations") async def get_escalations(request: Request): (no auth dependency)

brandme_core/config.py:338-344 — "governance": (AdapterRegistration(TrustComponent.AUTH_IDENTITY, _SIM, "...resolve_escalation trusts body reviewer_user_id", "Simulated — the reviewer's identity is not authenticated"),)
brandme_core/config.py:188-189 — Mode.SANDBOX: frozenset({AdapterKind.SANDBOX, AdapterKind.UNCONFIGURED}), Mode.PRODUCTION: frozenset({AdapterKind.REAL, AdapterKind.UNCONFIGURED})
brandme-governance/governance_console/main.py:14-16 — from brandme_core.boot import guard / BRANDME_MODE = guard("governance")
docker-compose.yml:138-143 — governance: profiles: [legacy] ... preflight --service governance && exec uvicorn main:app
preconditions: Service running (BRANDME_MODE=demo|development) and network reachability to port 8006.
expected: Only an authenticated operator with a reviewer role can resolve an escalation; the approver identity comes from the authenticated principal.
observed: Any caller can POST a decision naming any reviewer_user_id and clear escalated_to_human; the escalation list is also unauthenticated. The approved flag is logged but not acted upon.
impact: In development stacks, escalations can be closed by anyone and attributed to arbitrary reviewers, corrupting the audit trail; strict modes cannot boot this service at all, so the governance workflow is effectively unavailable in production.
recommended_fix: Add an authenticated operator principal (gateway-signed assertion or OIDC with a reviewer role) and derive human_approver_id from it; refuse body-supplied identities; then move the registration from LEGACY_SIMULATED_ADAPTERS to an audited process.
acceptance_test: POST /governance/escalations/{id}/decision without credentials returns 401; with a reviewer principal the AuditLog human_approver_id equals the principal's member id, never the body value; a test asserts guard('governance') passes in sandbox.

title: Brain returns a success-shaped result with fabricated stub_ chain hashes whenever the orchestrator call fails
severity_rationale: Silent integrity failure: in the default compose profile the orchestrator is not started, so every allowed scan in the development stack takes this fallback and reports status ok with fake anchors. Refused in strict modes by the boot guard, so the production impact is availability (brain cannot boot), not fraud.
evidence: brandme-core/brain/main.py:156-165 — except Exception as e: ... return {"status": "ok", "scan_id": ..., "cardano_tx_hash": "stub_" + str(uuid.uuid4())[:16], "midnight_tx_hash": "stub_" + ...
brandme-core/brain/main.py:278 — await call_orchestrator_commit(scan_packet, request_id, app.state.http_client) (return value discarded)
docker-compose.yml:24-26 — Profiles: default = emulators + migrate + brain + policy + gateway + consumer-domains + consumer. `--profile legacy` adds orchestrator/cube/agents/governance.
brandme-core/orchestrator/main.py:91-92 — transfer_id = str(uuid4()) / blockchain_tx_hash = f"cardano_tx_{transfer_id[:16]}"
brandme-core/orchestrator/worker.py:151-152 — "cardano_tx_hash": "tx_cardano_" + cardano_hash[:16], "midnight_tx_hash": "tx_midnight_" + midnight_hash[:16],

brandme_core/config.py:262-277 — "brain": (AdapterRegistration(TrustComponent.CHAIN_CARDANO, _SIM, "brandme-core/brain/main.py call_orchestrator_commit fallback", "Simulated — no blockchain transaction was made"),), "orchestrator": (...
preconditions: BRANDME_MODE=demo|development; orchestrator unreachable or returning an error.
expected: A failed commit is surfaced as a failure (or 'unavailable') and never as an anchored scan.
observed: The fallback returns status ok and random stub_ hashes; the caller ignores the commit result entirely, so intent_resolve reports scan_resolved regardless.
impact: Development evidence and demos can show anchored scans that were never committed; consumers of the brain response cannot distinguish a committed scan from a dropped one.
recommended_fix: Return an explicit failure/unavailable status from call_orchestrator_commit, propagate it into the intent_resolve response, and never synthesize hash fields; keep the simulated label only on outputs produced by an actual simulated adapter.
acceptance_test: With the orchestrator stopped, POST /intent/resolve for an allowed scan returns policy_decision allow with commit_status unavailable and no *_tx_hash fields; a unit test asserts no 'stub_' string is ever emitted.

title: Project MCP config auto-installs an unpinned npm package at session start and passes an API key on the command line
severity_rationale: Code execution on every contributor's workstation from an unpinned registry package (npx -y ...@latest) is a real supply-chain vector, and the key argument is visible in process listings. Limited to developer machines and to users who approve the project MCP server, so not High.
evidence: .mcp.json:4-9 — "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@21st-dev/magic@latest", "API_KEY=\"${MAGIC_API_KEY}\""]
.claude/settings.json:4-9 — "SessionStart": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh"}]}]
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh:21-38 — while IFS= read -r line ... printf "export %s='%s'\n" "$key" "$escaped" >> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE" (exports every line of .claude/.env.local)
docs/build/security/credential-manifest.yaml (MAGIC_API_KEY entry) — '.mcp.json passes the key as a command-line argument to an unpinned @21st-dev/magic@latest, where process listings can show it.'
preconditions: A contributor opens the repo in Claude Code and approves the project-scoped MCP server; .claude/.env.local exists.
expected: Dev tooling pins an exact package version (or vendors it) and passes secrets via environment, not argv.
observed: @latest with -y (no prompt) and the key in argv; the SessionStart hook exports all of .claude/.env.local into the session environment with no allowlist of variable names.
impact: A compromised or hijacked @21st-dev/magic release executes on developer machines with the developer's privileges and credentials; the API key is exposed to other local processes.
recommended_fix: Pin @21st-dev/magic to an exact version (and ideally an integrity hash via a lockfile-based launcher), pass MAGIC_API_KEY through env, and make the hook export only an allowlisted set of variable names.
acceptance_test: grep -c '@latest' .mcp.json returns 0; `ps` while the server runs shows no API_KEY= argument; the hook test exports only MAGIC_API_KEY.

title: Policy service defines two handlers for the same routes; the shadowed copies are permissive and reference an undefined helper
severity_rationale: Starlette matches the first registered route, so the permissive duplicates are dead today; any reordering or deletion of the first handler would silently activate a transfer check that never verifies ownership. Service is internal, unauthenticated by design, and strict modes refuse it.
evidence: brandme-core/policy/main.py:203 — @app.post("/policy/canViewFace")
brandme-core/policy/main.py:548 — @app.post("/policy/canViewFace") (second definition, payload: dict)
brandme-core/policy/main.py:577-581 — consent = await fetch_owner_and_consent(viewer_id, cube_id, request_id, app.state.http_client) (fetch_owner_and_consent is not defined anywhere in the module)
brandme-core/policy/main.py:331 — @app.post("/policy/canTransferOwnership")
brandme-core/policy/main.py:637-667 — second @app.post("/policy/canTransferOwnership") ... if price and price > 10000: decision = "escalate" else: decision = "allow" (no ownership lookup)
brandme_core/config.py:323-328 — "policy": (AdapterRegistration(TrustComponent.AUTH_IDENTITY, _SIM, "...canViewFace/canTransferOwnership trust payload IDs", ...),)
preconditions: None for the dead-code hazard; activation requires a future edit that removes or reorders the first handlers.
expected: One handler per route; ownership transfers verified against provenance.
observed: Duplicate decorators; the second canViewFace would raise NameError, the second canTransferOwnership allows any transfer under 10000.
impact: Latent authorization bypass and maintenance hazard; also makes the module's behaviour depend on definition order.
recommended_fix: Delete the second definitions (lines 548-682) and add a startup assertion/test that every route path+method is registered once.
acceptance_test: A test enumerates app.routes and asserts no duplicate (path, methods); grep -c 'canTransferOwnership' brandme-core/policy/main.py returns 1.

title: GitHub Actions pinned by major tag rather than commit SHA (12 of 13 distinct actions)
severity_rationale: Mutable tags allow a compromised upstream action to run in CI with contents:read plus (in build-images) a long-lived cloud key. The workflows are otherwise least-privilege and third-party scanners are SHA/digest pinned, so Low.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:67 — uses: actions/checkout@v4
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:366 — uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:345 — uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:561 — uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25 # v0.36.0 (the one SHA-pinned action)
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:544 — aquasec/trivy:0.75.0@sha256:af6acf9a6b85dfe389a1941505c0ce9efef52a4719635e1a962f022a3d855daa (digest-pinned image)
preconditions: Upstream tag moved to malicious code (historical precedent: tj-actions/changed-files 2025).
expected: All third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs with a version comment, refreshed by Dependabot.
observed: actions/checkout, setup-node, setup-python, pnpm/action-setup, upload-artifact, cache, docker/*, google-github-actions/*, github/codeql-action pinned by tag.
impact: Tag hijack of any of these runs arbitrary code in CI; in build-images this coincides with the GCP_SA_KEY secret.
recommended_fix: Pin every uses: to a commit SHA (with `# vX.Y.Z` comment) and add .github/dependabot.yml for github-actions updates.
acceptance_test: grep -E 'uses: [^@]+@v[0-9]' .github/workflows/*.yml returns nothing.

title: No CODEOWNERS and no Dependabot configuration; branch protection cannot be verified from code
severity_rationale: Absent review-ownership and automated dependency updates weaken change control for a repo whose main-branch pushes publish images; cannot be confirmed as exploitable from code alone.
evidence: .github/ (directory listing) — only scripts/smoke-image.sh and workflows/*.yml exist; no CODEOWNERS, no dependabot.yml
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:401-405 — if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && vars.BM_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true' / environment: sandbox
preconditions: N/A
expected: CODEOWNERS covering .github/, brandme-gateway/src/middleware, brandme_core/mcp, brandme-infra; Dependabot for npm, pip and github-actions; required reviews and status checks on main (unknowable here).
observed: Neither file exists. Branch protection, required reviewers, tag protection and the 'sandbox' environment's protection rules are GitHub settings not present in the repository and were not assessed.
impact: A single maintainer push to main publishes images; no automatic advisories for the 17 requirements files or pnpm lock beyond the CI Trivy gate.
recommended_fix: Add CODEOWNERS and dependabot.yml; document the branch/tag protection and environment approvers in docs/build/deploy and have an admin export the settings for the audit.
acceptance_test: Files exist and a PR touching .github/workflows requests the owning team; a repo-settings export shows required reviews on main and protected v* tags.

title: Legacy per-service Dockerfiles run as root on floating python:3.11-slim tags and the Makefile pushes :latest images
severity_rationale: These Dockerfiles are not used by CI (which builds the hardened multi-stage images) but remain the target of make build-*/push-* and could be picked up by a human operator; Helm refuses :latest, limiting deployment impact.
evidence: brandme-core/brain/Dockerfile:1 — FROM python:3.11-slim (no USER directive in file)
brandme-governance/governance_console/Dockerfile:1 — FROM python:3.11-slim (no USER directive in file)
Makefile:212 — docker build -t gcr.io/brandme/gateway:latest ./brandme-gateway
Makefile:238 — docker push gcr.io/brandme/gateway:latest
brandme-core/Dockerfile:89,106 — FROM python:3.11.15-slim AS runtime ... USER 10001:10001 (the CI-built image)
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:348 — file: ./brandme-${{ matrix.service }}/Dockerfile
brandme-infra/helm/brandme/templates/_helpers.tpl:92 — {{- if or (eq $img.tag "latest") (contains "REPLACE_ME" $img.tag) -}} (fail)
preconditions: An operator uses make build-*/push-* or docker builds a per-service Dockerfile.
expected: One hardened Dockerfile per deployable, non-root, pinned base digest; no :latest publishing path.
observed: Seven legacy Dockerfiles (brain, policy, orchestrator, identity, knowledge, compliance, governance_console) run as root; Makefile targets push :latest to a different registry path (gcr.io/brandme/) than CI (gcr.io/lux-realestate-app/).
impact: Confusing, drift-prone build surface; a root container image could be deployed by hand.
recommended_fix: Delete the legacy Dockerfiles and Makefile build/push targets or point them at the CI Dockerfiles with digest tags.
acceptance_test: find . -name Dockerfile | xargs grep -L '^USER' returns nothing; grep -c ':latest' Makefile returns 0.

title: Gateway exits immediately on SIGTERM without draining in-flight requests
severity_rationale: Kubernetes rolling updates will cut connections mid-request; no data-integrity impact on the identity store (Spanner transactions), but failed mutations during deploys. The chain service shows the correct pattern.
evidence: brandme-gateway/src/index.ts:106-107 — process.on('SIGTERM', () => process.exit(0)); process.on('SIGINT', () => process.exit(0));

brandme-chain/src/index.ts:82-88 — const shutdown = () => { ... server.close(() => resolve()) ... setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 10_000).unref();
preconditions: Pod termination during traffic.
expected: server.close(), wait for in-flight requests with a bounded timeout, close Spanner/NATS, then exit.
observed: Immediate exit.
impact: Spurious 5xx/connection resets during rollouts; retries of non-idempotent /scan publishes.
recommended_fix: Mirror brandme-chain's shutdown handler; add a readiness probe that flips before draining.
acceptance_test: Integration test: send SIGTERM during a slow request; the request completes and the process exits 0 within the timeout.

title: Gateway logs the full NATS connection URL, which may embed credentials
severity_rationale: nats:// URLs commonly carry user:password; the pino redaction list does not cover a top-level `url` field. Only triggers when NATS_URL is set (legacy /scan path).
evidence: brandme-gateway/src/services/nats.ts:19 — logger.info({ url: config.natsUrl }, 'Connecting to NATS...');
brandme-gateway/src/config/logger.ts:13-41 — export const REDACT_PATHS = [ 'req.headers.authorization', ... '*.secret', '*.apiKey', '*.wallet', ]; (no 'url' / 'natsUrl')
preconditions: NATS_URL configured with inline credentials.
expected: Log host:port only, or redact userinfo.
observed: Whole URL logged at info.
impact: Broker credentials in log aggregation.
recommended_fix: Log `new URL(natsUrl).host` only; add 'url' and 'natsUrl' to REDACT_PATHS or strip userinfo.

preconditions: MIDNIGHT_NETWORK=preprod|mainnet with a Blockfrost token.

title: In-process, per-replica token-bucket rate limiting (documented) and a GKE TRUST_PROXY value that is not confirmed against a live cluster
severity_rationale: Limits multiply by replica count and reset on restart; X-Forwarded-For spoofing is prevented by default (trust proxy off, 'true' refused) and covered by a test, but a wrong hop count in production would let clients choose their own rate-limit key.
evidence: brandme-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts:24-30 — Storage is in memory, per process ... With N gateway replicas a client gets up to N times the budget and a restart resets all buckets
brandme-gateway/src/config/index.ts:53-56 — if (v === 'true') { ctx.addIssue({ ... message: 'TRUST_PROXY=true trusts any client-supplied X-Forwarded-For; set a hop count or proxy subnets' });
brandme-gateway/src/config/index.ts:40-44 — GKE Ingress ... so the GKE value is TRUST_PROXY=2. That comes from Google's documented header format, not from a live cluster: confirm req.ip
brandme-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimiter.test.ts:143-149 — it('honours X-Forwarded-For only for the configured proxy hops', ... toBe(429)
brandme-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts:149-152 — isEssentialAccess: READ_ONLY.has(req.method) || EXPORT_PATH.test(...) (per-member budget exempts all GETs)
preconditions: Multi-replica deployment; or an operator setting TRUST_PROXY higher than the real hop count.
expected: Shared store (Memorystore) before relying on limits for abuse/cost control; hop count validated against observed req.ip.
observed: As documented in code comments; no shared store exists.
impact: Abuse control weaker than headline numbers suggest; brute-force of /session/dev or bearer guessing is only IP-limited.
recommended_fix: Add a Redis-backed limiter for sandbox/production and record the verified TRUST_PROXY hop count in the deploy packet with a probe.
acceptance_test: Two replicas share one bucket (integration test); deploy checklist includes a req.ip verification step with evidence.

title: Replay caches for gateway-signed assertions are in-memory per process (single-replica assumption)
severity_rationale: jti single-use is enforced per process; with multiple consumer-domain or commerce replicas, a captured assertion (<=60 s) could be replayed against another replica. The code and config state the one-replica assumption explicitly.
evidence: brandme_core/domains/persona/assertion.py:80-87 — with self._lock: if len(self._seen) >= REPLAY_CACHE_MAX or jti in self._seen: ... if jti in self._seen: raise AssertionRejected("replayed")

brandme_core/mcp/authz.py:199-203 — with self._lock: self._seen = {j: e for j, e in self._seen.items() if e >= now - CLOCK_SKEW} / if claims["jti"] in self._seen: raise AuthError(401, "invalid_token", "executor assertion replayed")
brandme_core/config.py:509-510 — "... jti single-use within the process (in-memory cache; the chart runs one replica), environment)"
preconditions: More than one replica of the verifying service and an attacker able to capture an assertion on the internal hop.
expected: Shared replay store or mTLS on the internal hop when scaling out.
observed: Process-local dict with lock; documented assumption.
impact: Bounded replay window on internal hops at scale.
recommended_fix: Back the jti cache with Spanner/Redis (or enforce replicas=1 in the chart with a comment) before scaling.
acceptance_test: Chart values pin replicas: 1 for assertion-verifying services, or an integration test shows a replayed jti rejected across two replicas.

title: Internal Python services (brain, policy, orchestrator, identity, knowledge, compliance) have no caller authentication and trust identity fields in request bodies/paths
severity_rationale: Flat trust inside the service network; every one of these is registered as a simulated AUTH_IDENTITY/chain adapter and cannot boot in sandbox/production, and compose publishes their ports only on the local host. Recorded for completeness since brain and policy run in the default development stack.

docker-compose.yml:101-108 — brain ... ports: ["8000:8000"] / policy ... ports: ["8001:8001"]
preconditions: Development stack; attacker on the host network.
expected: Service-to-service authentication (the pattern already used by read_api/exports: per-service bearer + X-Subject-Ref, or gateway-signed assertions).
observed: None on the legacy services; the newer consumer-domain, read API and export API hops are authenticated.

recommended_fix: Either retire the legacy services or front them with the DomainAssertionVerifier; bind compose ports to 127.0.0.1.

title: Internal read/export APIs authorize on a service bearer plus a client-chosen X-Subject-Ref header
severity_rationale: Any holder of the per-service token can read any subject's inventory/exports by setting the header; this is the documented, open design decision (PD-07) and the token is confined to the gateway, so Low.
evidence: brandme_core/read_api/app.py:73-81 — token = (config.rights_token if request.url.path.startswith("/rights/") else config.privacy_token ...) ... hmac.compare_digest(auth[0].encode(), f"Bearer {token}".encode()) ... subjects = request.headers.getlist("x-subject-ref")

brandme-gateway/src/middleware/mode.ts:69-74 — for (const t of tokens) if (t.urlSet && !t.value) v.push(`${t.token} is required when ${t.url} is set`); ... must be distinct
preconditions: Compromise of the gateway's service token (Secret Manager or gateway process).
expected: Per-request signed subject assertion (as the consumer-domain hop already does) so a leaked token alone cannot name arbitrary subjects.
observed: Static token + header; tokens must be distinct per backend (good) and are never browser-exposed.
impact: Token compromise equals full cross-member read of rights/privacy data on that backend.
recommended_fix: Adopt the ES256 principal assertion (DomainAssertionVerifier) for read_api and privacy_exports; keep the bearer as transport auth.
acceptance_test: A request with a valid service token but a subject not in the signed assertion returns 401.
